I think there needs to be more access to level mats in an intuitive way, or I'm worried about new player retention. The inflated numbers definitely do make it a struggle in a way that's not fun. There are already really neat mechanics that require approaching each fight differently, so I'm a bit unclear on why they couldn't have worked around needing to have such ridiculously high numbers that it locks out almost all damage dealers. With flat damage, there's not really any way to account for the inflated HP outside of scaling those flat numbers up to a point where all other content in the game becomes utterly trivial, except to drop the inflated numbers down to something where in a turn a flat damage character can do about as much as a %HP character. From what I can tell, it seems like some numbers weren't balanced so they just decided to take numbers effectively out of the equation entirely except when expressed as a percentage. Instead of rebalancing via scaling the bosses up a *bit* and then scaling up the older characters who fell behind to be more in line with new ones, without setting the new ones to make all other content trivial.

As it stands, getting limited characters makes at least the early game *painfully* trivial, which never needed to happen in the first place with a little more of an eye to balancing and less of one to making the newer character stronger than the last one so people will pull for them, instead of letting the art/VA/abilities/flavor text all speak for itself.
